A semi-humorous compilation of complaints from the UNIX-HATERS mailing list, edited by Simson Garfinkel, Daniel Weise, and Steven Strassmann.
The book examines Unix's command-line interface, design philosophy, system administration, networking, and X Window System through the frustrations of its users.
Published by IDG Books in 1994, with a foreword by Person/Don Norman and an anti-foreword by Person/Dennis Ritchie.

1 Unix — The World's First Computer Virus
Why it is included:: Establishes the book's thesis that Unix's success came from historical circumstance and institutional momentum as much as from sound design.
1 Unix — The World's First Computer Virus
2 Welcome, New User! — Like Russian Roulette with Six Bullets Loaded
Why it is included:: Shows how Unix turns ordinary first encounters into avoidable failures and treats user confusion as a rite of passage.
2 Welcome, New User! — Like Russian Roulette with Six Bullets Loaded
Why it is included:: Explains why Unix's steep learning curve is not merely a user problem but a consequence of knowledge being left implicit or poorly communicated.
4 Mail — Don't Talk to Me, I'm Not a Typewriter!
Why it is included:: Demonstrates how a supposedly basic everyday service becomes a sprawling operational hazard when reliability and usability are secondary concerns.
4 Mail — Don't Talk to Me, I'm Not a Typewriter!
5 Snoozenet — I Post, Therefore I Am
Why it is included:: Extends the critique from Unix software to the social and network systems built on it, where scale magnifies disorder instead of solving it.
5 Snoozenet — I Post, Therefore I Am
Why it is included:: Reveals how Unix's apparently simple terminal model accumulated historical accidents and became a source of recurring complexity.
7 The X-Windows Disaster — How to Make a 50-MIPS Workstation Run Like a 4.77MHz IBM PC
Why it is included:: Shows that Unix's problems persist when its conventions are transferred into graphical computing: flexibility becomes layers, latency, and poor usability.
7 The X-Windows Disaster — How to Make a 50-MIPS Workstation Run Like a 4.77MHz IBM PC
8 csh, pipes, and find — Power Tools for Power Fools
Why it is included:: Attacks Unix's celebrated power-user tools at their source, showing how composability can shift complexity and risk onto the operator.
8 csh, pipes, and find — Power Tools for Power Fools
9 Programming — Hold Still, This Won't Hurt a Bit
Why it is included:: Argues that Unix's reputation as a programmer's system hides brittle tools and workflows that make software development harder to reason about.
9 Programming — Hold Still, This Won't Hurt a Bit
Why it is included:: Connects Unix's tool culture to the dominant systems language of its era and asks whether added features actually improve reliability or comprehension.
Why it is included:: Makes visible the human and organizational cost that Unix's low purchase price and apparent flexibility conceal.
12 Security — Oh, I'm Sorry, Sir, Go Ahead, I Didn't Realize You Were Root
Why it is included:: Shows that Unix's assumptions about trusted users and discretionary privilege become dangerous when systems are networked and widely shared.
12 Security — Oh, I'm Sorry, Sir, Go Ahead, I Didn't Realize You Were Root
13 The File System — Sure It Corrupts Your Files, But Look How Fast It Is!
Why it is included:: Brings the critique down to Unix's core storage abstraction, where elegant simplicity can fail at the point where users most need their data protected.
13 The File System — Sure It Corrupts Your Files, But Look How Fast It Is!
Why it is included:: Serves as the book's culminating systems case study: networking exposes and amplifies the reliability, consistency, and security weaknesses of Unix foundations.
